transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Well, doctor, it’s… it’s this thing that happens when I’m driving toward Miami, especially when I get to one of those long bridges. I can be doing all right up until then, and then the moment my car is actually on the bridge, my chest tightens right up, and my hands just clamp down on the steering wheel like I can’t loosen them.

And it’s not just that I feel nervous. It’s this sudden, awful certainty that I have to get off the bridge immediately, right then, except of course there’s nowhere to go. I know that sounds… maybe dramatic, but in the moment it feels completely real and urgent. That’s what finally made me come in, because I can’t seem to just talk myself out of it.
Has this kind of reaction ever happened to you anywhere other than on bridges, or is it something that only seems to happen specifically when you're driving across them?

It really seems to be the bridges themselves, especially those long ones on the way toward Miami. I can be driving along and feel more or less like myself, and then when the car actually gets onto the bridge, it’s like my body reacts before I can reason with it.

My chest tightens, my hands grip the steering wheel so hard, and I get this terrible feeling that I need to get off the bridge immediately. Not just “I’d rather not be here,” but like I have to get off right then. And of course that’s the awful part, because there’s nowhere to go once I’m on it. So I don’t think it’s happening everywhere I drive—it’s specifically when I’m crossing those bridges.
Have you ever had similar feelings of panic or an overwhelming need to escape in other situations, like being in crowded places, open spaces, or public transportation?

Not really in the same way, no. I mean, I can be uncomfortable in busy places sometimes the way anyone can, but that isn’t what this feels like. It’s very tied to those bridges and that stretch over the water.

The frustrating part is that I know, in my sensible mind, those bridges have been there for years. People drive over them all day long, every day, and nothing happens to them. I can say that to myself quite clearly. But when I picture myself driving over all that open water, or when I’m actually on the bridge, the fear just feels so much larger than the real danger. It’s like my reason knows one thing, but my body believes something else entirely.
Outside of being on those bridges, have you ever experienced this same intense fear or panic in other specific situations—like flying, being in enclosed spaces, or maybe even standing on high places?

No, not really those other things. I mean, I don’t love the idea of certain situations, but nothing catches me the way those bridges do.

And that’s part of what bothers me, because I can sit here, perfectly calmly, and tell you I know those bridges have been there for years. I know plenty of people cross them every single day without anything happening. I’m not confused about that. But when I think about being the one driving over all that open water, the fear just gets so much bigger than the actual danger. It feels out of proportion, but in the moment it still feels very real.
